record.paper_title: Bootstrap Algebraic Multigrid: status report, open problems, and outlook
record.original_question: For non-Hermitian problems, how can restriction R and interpolation P be constructed and tied together locally so that the Galerkin coarse-grid matrix remains suitable for multigrid correction and does not become singular or cause divergence through overcorrection when small singular values or eigenvalues are underestimated on coarse levels?

evidence.quote: Thus, it is possible that the Galerkin coarse level operator can have a zero eigenvalue, even when the fine-level matrix does not.
We have observed in practice that in such cases, the resulting Galerkin method can diverge.

Thus, although the BAMG process provides techniques for constructing restriction R and interpolation P, each in their own setup scheme, these processes must be carefully tied together locally in order to obtain a suitable Galerkin coarse-grid matrix.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A \in \mathbb{C}^{n 	imes n}$ be a (possibly non-Hermitian) nonsingular matrix associated with a fine grid, and consider a two-level multigrid scheme with a coarse space of dimension $n_c < n$ defined by a restriction operator $R \in \mathbb{C}^{n_c 	imes n}$ and an interpolation operator $P \in \mathbb{C}^{n 	imes n_c}$. The Galerkin coarse-grid operator is defined as
$$A_c = R\,A\,P \in \mathbb{C}^{n_c 	imes n_c}.$$
When $A$ is non-Hermitian, $R$ and $P$ may be chosen independently (typically using approximations to right and left near-kernel modes of $A$). It can happen that $A_c$ is singular or has eigenvalues/singular values whose magnitudes are much smaller than those of the corresponding modes of $A$, and this leads to divergence of the two-level correction step $x \leftarrow x + P A_c^{-1} R\,(b - A x)$ through overcorrection.

Provide a constructive procedure that, given $A$ and given algorithms which separately produce candidate operators $R$ and $P$ from approximations to left and right near-kernel modes of $A$, locally couples these constructions so that the resulting Galerkin coarse operator $A_c = R A P$ is provably nonsingular and the resulting two-level iteration is non-divergent. In particular, derive sufficient local conditions linking the rows of $R$ to the columns of $P$ on each aggregate or coarse degree of freedom which guarantee that small singular values and eigenvalues of $A$ are not underestimated on the coarse level, and prove convergence (or non-divergence) of the resulting multigrid correction.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of robustly constructing coupled R and P for non-Hermitian algebraic multigrid (so that the Galerkin coarse operator remains nonsingular and avoids overcorrection) is a recognized open challenge in bootstrap/adaptive AMG. Subsequent work on non-Hermitian/non-symmetric AMG (e.g., AIR, lAIR, multigrid for Markov chains) provides partial heuristics, but no general procedure with rigorous guarantees has been established.

status_evidence.title: Bootstrap Algebraic Multigrid: status report, open problems, and outlook
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems regarding stable non-Hermitian RAP and tying R and P together locally to avoid singular Galerkin operators and divergence.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is identified as open in the bootstrap AMG status report.
